fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Internal Drive Aisle; Pool Area; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage; Pedestrian Walkways
fr.considerations: Long Driveway; Single Access Point; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations: Confirming address numbering is clearly visible from the access road and street frontage could significantly improve responder navigation, particularly given the length of the driveway and single point of entry. Ensuring the driveway and internal drive aisle remain clear of parked vehicles and obstructions would support apparatus maneuvering and positioning near the main building. Identifying and communicating any secondary access options through the perimeter fencing to responding units in advance may assist when the primary access point is restricted. The open green space and pool area could serve as effective staging zones, and sharing that information with the local fire department through a pre-incident plan would support operational coordination during an emergency response.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Heavy Ground Vegetation; Continuous Grass Cover; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Irrigated Landscape; Long Driveway; Vegetated Access Route; Open Terrain; Limited Defensible Space
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing vegetation density immediately surrounding the structure, including brush and other vegetation in direct contact with or adjacent to exterior walls and attachments, could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce the opportunity for fire to reach the structure. Creating and maintaining separation between shrubs, trees, and ground-level fuels near the structure may reduce fuel continuity across the property. Where continuous grass cover and heavy ground vegetation are present, periodic mowing or removal during dry seasonal periods could reduce surface fuel loads. Managing vegetation along the length of the driveway and access route would support firefighter access and improve evacuation conditions. Maintaining the irrigated landscaping near the structure as a managed, lower-fuel zone could further support a functional defensible space perimeter. Given the limited defensible space observed, prioritizing vegetation management closest to the structure and along the primary access route would provide the most immediate benefit to overall wildfire resilience and suppression support.
